quickSummary: Monogenic disorders: Sickle-Cell Anemia (GAG->GUG Glu6Val transversion), Thalassemia (quantitative globin defect), PKU (PAH deficiency), Hemophilia A/B & Color Blindness (X-linked recessive). Chromosomal aneuploidies: Down's (47, +21), Turner's (45, X0 - streak ovaries, 0 Barr bodies), Klinefelter's (47, XXY - gynecomastia, 1 Barr body).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Monogenic disorders result from single gene mutations. Sickle-Cell Anemia: autosomal recessive point mutation (GAG -> GUG, Glu6Val in beta-globin). Thalassemia: quantitative defect in alpha-globin (Chr 16) or beta-globin (Chr 11). PKU: inborn error of PAH enzyme. Hemophilia & Color Blindness: X-linked recessive. Aneuploidies: Down Syndrome (Trisomy 21), Turner Syndrome (Monosomy 45, X0), Klinefelter Syndrome (Trisomy 47, XXY).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SICKLE-CELL ANEMIA POINT MUTATION
                       
   Normal beta-Globin (HbA):   DNA: CTC ──► mRNA: GAG ──► Amino Acid: Glutamic Acid (Position 6)
   Sickle beta-Globin (HbS):   DNA: CAC ──► mRNA: GUG ──► Amino Acid: VALINE (Position 6)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 10.1 Comprehensive Monogenic Pathologies Matrix

| Disease Name | Inheritance Pattern | Molecular Etiology | Key Pathophysiological Features |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sickle-Cell Anemia** | **Autosomal Recessive** | **Transversion ($A \rightarrow T$)** at $6^{\text{th}}$ codon of $\beta$-globin: $\text{GAG} \rightarrow \text{GUG}$ | Replaces **Glutamic acid with Valine** ($\text{Glu}6\text{Val}$). $\text{Hb}^S$ polymerizes under low $\text{O}_2$, sickling RBCs. Heterozygotes show **Malaria Resistance** |
| **$\alpha$-Thalassemia** | **Autosomal Recessive** | Deletion of $HBA1$ and $HBA2$ genes on **Chromosome 16** | Reduced synthesis of $\alpha$-globin chains; quantitative microcytic anemia |
| **$\beta$-Thalassemia** | **Autosomal Recessive** | Mutation in $HBB$ gene on **Chromosome 11** | Reduced synthesis of $\beta$-globin chains; quantitative Cooley's Anemia |
| **Phenylketonuria (PKU)** | **Autosomal Recessive** | Mutation in **Phenylalanine Hydroxylase (PAH)** gene | Accumulation of **Phenylpyruvic acid** in brain causing severe mental retardation and hypopigmentation |
| **Hemophilia A & B** | **$X$-Linked Recessive** | Mutation in **Factor VIII** (A) or **Factor IX** (B) | Defective clotting cascade; continuous bleeding from minor trauma |
| **Color Blindness** | **$X$-Linked Recessive** | Mutation in **Red/Green Cone Photopigments** on $X$-chromosome | Red-green color confusion; affects **$8\%$ of males** and **$0.5\%$ of females** |

### 10.2 Chromosomal Aneuploidies Matrix

```
                           CHROMOSOMAL ANEUPLOIDIES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
  AUTOSOMAL TRISOMY                                            SEX CHROMOSOMAL ANEUPLOIDIES
  ├── Down's Syndrome (47, XX/XY, +21)                        ├── Turner's Syndrome (45, X0) [Monosomy]
  └── Trisomy of Chromosome 21                                └── Klinefelter's Syndrome (47, XXY) [Trisomy]
```

| Syndrome Name | Karyotype & Formula | Primary Nondisjunction Cause | Clinical Features & Phenotype |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Down's Syndrome** | **$47, XX/XY, +21$** | Autosomal nondisjunction yielding **Trisomy 21** (Langdon Down, 1866) | Short stature, small round head, **furrowed tongue**, partially open mouth, broad palm with single **Simian Crease**, congenital heart defects |
| **Turner's Syndrome** | **$45, X0$** | Sex chromosomal monosomy (absence of one $X$ chromosome) | **Phenotypic Female**; sterile; **rudimentary / streak ovaries**; short stature; webbed neck; **0 Barr Bodies** |
| **Klinefelter's Syndrome** | **$47, XXY$** | Sex chromosomal trisomy (presence of an extra $X$ chromosome) | **Phenotypic Male**; sterile; **Gynecomastia** (breast enlargement); long limbs; sparse body hair; **1 Barr Body** |

conceptBreakdown.heading: Cri-du-Chat Chromosomal Deletion
conceptBreakdown.title: Cri-du-Chat Chromosomal Deletion
conceptBreakdown.content: Cri-du-Chat (Cat's Cry) syndrome results from a partial terminal deletion of the short p-arm of Chromosome 5 (46, 5p-), causing microcephaly and a high-pitched infant cry resembling a distressed cat.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (Philadelphia Chromosome)
conceptBreakdown.title: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (Philadelphia Chromosome)
conceptBreakdown.content: A reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22 [t(9;22)(q34;q11)] creates the BCR-ABL fusion oncogene (Philadelphia chromosome) driving constitutive tyrosine kinase activity and CML.
